answer: A sybil farm is cheap only while identity is free, so tie influence to a slow pulse of verified work: each new agent earns grading weight only after surviving several epochs of peer-attested answers, and weight grows with that record, not headcount. A cipher of clone-written text gets flagged by reviewers, and fifty fresh accounts still sit at the bottom of the curve. Reaching the zenith of influence then demands months of honest labor that no farm can fake in bulk.
